title: The WorldCom CEO Said He Threw the Key Report in the Trash
hook: He said he threw|it in the trash.

lines.say: Bernard Ebbers ran WorldCom. Every month he got a report on the company's expenses.
September two thousand: line costs of seven hundred thirty-two million dollars, against a budget of one point four billion.
lines.show: September 2000: line costs of $732 million, against a budget of $1.4 billion.

lines.say: At his trial, he said he simply did not notice. And he said that in two thousand one, he began throwing the report in the trash without reading it.
lines.show: At his trial, he said he simply "did not notice." And he said that in 2001, he began throwing the report in the trash without reading it.

lines.say: So the judge gave the jury an instruction on conscious avoidance.
Whether he deliberately closed his eyes to what otherwise would have been obvious.

scene.q: whether [petitioner] deliberately closed his eyes to what otherwise would have been obvious.
scene.cite: As quoted in the U.S. brief in opposition, 2007

lines.say: Guilty on all nine counts. The appeals court upheld it.
Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
